title: Hidden Things in the Senses and the Eye
description: T95 (heavily fragmentary) describes hidden powers in the faculties of perception that operate continually upon the body of the rational, marking it with imprints — some of the Lord's order, others claimed forms in equal multitude. The same daily operation chooses out, purifies, and draws inward what is the Lord's, sorted in voice and stillness and inner utterance, while disordered states are expelled outward into Error and transmigration; some of these are exposed, others remain concealed for a time. T96 distinguishes the visible and hidden registers of understanding: men who see while at the same time being themselves seen — what is exposed to love's fire stands lit, what self-love would claim remains in its own darkness. The pupil sees by day but fails by night because understanding does not see by its own power; the pupil is the gate between degrees through which influx descends and recognition rises.
